from pyscf import gto, scf, agf2, df
import numpy as np

# Define molecule
mol = gto.Mole()
mol.atom = '''
O  0.000000  0.000000  0.000000
H  0.000000 -0.757160  0.586260
H  0.000000  0.757160  0.586260
'''
mol.basis = 'cc-pvdz'
mol.charge = 0
mol.spin = 0
mol.build()

# RHF with density fitting and specified convergence tolerance and auxiliary basis
mf = scf.RHF(mol).density_fit(auxbasis='cc-pvdz-ri')
mf.conv_tol = 1e-10
mf.kernel()

# AGF2 calculation with density fitting and specified convergence tolerance
gf2 = agf2.AGF2(mf, nmom=(6,6), verbose=0)
gf2.conv_tol = 1e-7
gf2.kernel()

# Print first three ionization potentials and electron affinities
ip = -gf2.ip[:3]
ea = -gf2.ea[:3]
print("First three ionization potentials (eV):")
print(ip * 27.2114)
print("First three electron affinities (eV):")
print(ea * 27.2114)

# Calculate MO-basis density matrix
dm = gf2.make_rdm1()

# AO to MO transformation for dipole integrals
dip_ao = mol.intor_symmetric('int1e_r', comp=3)
mo_coeff = mf.mo_coeff
dip_mo = np.einsum('xuv,ua,va->xab', dip_ao, mo_coeff, mo_coeff)

# Dipole moment (electronic part)
mu_elec = np.einsum('xii->x', np.einsum('xab,ab->xab', dip_mo, dm))

# Nuclear dipole moment
charges = mol.atom_charges()
coords = mol.atom_coords()
mu_nuc = np.dot(charges, coords)

# Total dipole moment (nuclear - electronic)
mu_tot = mu_nuc - mu_elec
mu_tot_debye = mu_tot * 2.541746

print("Dipole moment (Debye):")
print(mu_tot_debye)
